title: Ethiopian Honey Banana Dessert
community: Southern Ethiopia — the banana-growing region's simplest dessert
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Honey Banana — ripe bananas halved and pan-fried in a little oil until golden, then drizzled with Ethiopian honey, cardamom, and a squeeze of lemon. The simplest and most beloved Ethiopian sweet — three ingredients, ten minutes, completely satisfying.
longDesc: Ethiopian honey banana is the dessert of abundance — when bananas are ripe and honey is available, this combination requires almost no cooking and produces an extraordinary result. The bananas caramelise in the pan, the honey deepens their sweetness, and the cardamom adds complexity.
ingredients: // Optional: pinch of cinnamon, chopped nuts
steps: Heat oil or butter in a wide pan over medium heat.
Cook 3—4 minutes until golden and caramelised on the cut side.
chefTips: Very ripe bananas — the natural sugars are essential for caramelisation.
Add honey at the end — earlier and it burns.
Serve immediately — the caramelised bananas deflate quickly.
cookingScience: The cut surface of the banana undergoes Maillard reaction and caramelisation simultaneously — the amino acids in the banana flesh react with the natural sugars at the pan surface temperature, producing hundreds of complex flavour compounds. The honey added at the end caramelises rapidly due to its high fructose content.
sustainabilityTips: Southern Ethiopian bananas — grown without irrigation.
culturalNote: Ethiopian honey banana is the dessert that needs no occasion — made when bananas are at their most ripe and eaten with the simple joy of good ingredients combined with minimal intervention. It is the philosophy of Ethiopian cooking in its simplest form.
